trigger_or_context: You want to connect or get things going. You notice you are always the one who starts it.
short_term_function: Starting things keeps you two connected instead of letting it go quiet.
developmental_cost: You carry all the work of reaching out. You cannot tell if they would ever start on their own.
adaptive_alternative_1: If you notice you always start things, pause sometimes. Say you would like them to reach out too, then leave room to see if they do.
what_new_response_supports: You see if starting things can be shared, or stays only on you.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: They may not step up. You sit with the quiet while you wait.
context_conditions: Starting things is not bad. This is about balance, not about going cold.
review_reason: Meaning depends on the balance of who initiates; function is partly inferred.

trigger_or_context: A problem comes up. You notice you are always the one who steps in to fix it.
short_term_function: Fixing it keeps things running and stops the problem from just sitting there.
developmental_cost: You carry all the fixing. The other person never has to help, and you get worn out.
adaptive_alternative_1: When a problem comes up, pause before you jump in. Name it out loud and leave room for the other person to help fix it.
what_new_response_supports: You see if fixing problems can be shared, or stays only on you.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Problems may sit longer. They may not step in.
context_conditions: Some things really do need you. This is about not carrying every single thing alone.
review_reason: Function partly inferred; over-functioning maintains the one-sided load.

trigger_or_context: You have tried for a while and feel worn out. Nothing changed, so you stop putting in effort.
short_term_function: Stopping saves your energy after trying has not led to any change.
developmental_cost: The other person stops seeing what is wrong. The distance between you grows because no one is working on it.
adaptive_alternative_1: Instead of quietly stopping, name it. Say you have pulled back and why, and ask what would need to change.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if real change is still possible here, or not.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Nothing may change. You may have to face what that means.
context_conditions: If you have truly tried many times and named it, stepping back may be part of deciding, not just giving up.
review_reason: Can shade toward discernment after real repeated effort; context-sensitive.

trigger_or_context: Something feels unfair or one-sided. Instead of saying it, you add it to a list in your head.
short_term_function: Keeping score keeps a record of what feels unfair so it is not forgotten.
developmental_cost: The focus stays on old wrongs. It gets harder to move forward or feel close, and resentment grows.
adaptive_alternative_1: When something feels unfair, name that one thing out loud soon after. Ask for what you need instead of storing it.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if the unfair things can be worked on, instead of piling up.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Speaking up feels risky. They may not respond the way you hope.
context_conditions: Noticing unfairness is okay. This is about voicing it early instead of storing it all up.
review_reason: Function inferred from the Resentment context; keeping score maintains resentment.

trigger_or_context: You want to talk or connect. You notice you are always the one who texts first.
short_term_function: Texting first keeps the contact going instead of waiting and wondering.
developmental_cost: You carry all the reaching out. You cannot tell if they would text you on their own.
adaptive_alternative_1: Notice if you are always first. Sometimes wait and leave room to see if they reach out to you too.
what_new_response_supports: You see if the effort goes both ways, or only from you.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: They may not reach out. You sit with the quiet and the not-knowing.
context_conditions: Texting first is fine sometimes. This is about whether it is ever returned.
review_reason: Reciprocity function is partly inferred; meaning depends on the balance of effort.

trigger_or_context: You want to spend time together. You notice you are always the one making the plans.
short_term_function: Making the plans keeps you two seeing each other instead of nothing happening.
developmental_cost: You carry all the planning. You cannot tell if they would plan time with you.
adaptive_alternative_1: If you notice you plan everything, hold back sometimes. Leave room to see if they make a plan too.
what_new_response_supports: You see if making time together is shared, or only your job.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Plans may not happen. You sit with the not-knowing.
context_conditions: Making plans is fine. This is about whether it goes both ways.
review_reason: Reciprocity function is partly inferred; meaning depends on the balance of effort.

trigger_or_context: You put in a lot of effort with people and it feels one-sided, like you are chasing them.
developmental_cost: This is a feeling about the effort, not one clear action. There is no single behavior here to change yet.
review_reason: Outcome/feeling-level statement ("I feel like I'm chasing"); does not name one discrete alterable behavior.

trigger_or_context: You care about someone. You notice you keep giving more than you get back.
short_term_function: Giving more keeps the relationship going and keeps them close, at least from your side.
developmental_cost: You pour in more than comes back. You cannot tell if they would give more on their own, and you get drained.
adaptive_alternative_1: Notice how much they give back. Match your giving to what returns, instead of always giving more.
what_new_response_supports: You see if the giving can go both ways, or stays one-sided.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Giving less may feel wrong at first. You may see they do not step up.
context_conditions: Giving is good. This is about balance — you still get to be generous when it is mutual.
review_reason: Reciprocity function is partly inferred; meaning depends on the balance of effort.
